articleBody:
Converting a garage into an in-law suite, guest bedroom, or expanded living room is one of the most efficient ways to gain square footage, but skipping essential preparation can stall your project or trigger code violations.

- [ ] Zoning and parking verification — Confirm your local municipality or HOA allows converting vehicle parking into habitable living space.
- [ ] Stamped architectural plans — Prepare scaled layout drawings showing structural framing, window egress dimensions, and electrical layouts.
- [ ] Official building and trade permits — Ensure structural, electrical, mechanical, and plumbing permits are secured before construction starts.
- [ ] Concrete slab moisture test — Test the garage slab for moisture vapor emission to avoid damaged flooring and interior mold issues.
- [ ] Finished ceiling height measurement — Measure from the slab to the joists to guarantee finished headroom meets the residential minimum.
- [ ] Emergency egress window sizing — Confirm bedroom plans include a window with clear opening dimensions required for emergency exit.
- [ ] Dedicated HVAC design — Calculate heating and cooling loads to provide independent, properly sized temperature and humidity control.
- [ ] Electrical panel capacity review — Verify your main electrical service can handle added circuits, lighting, and climate systems.
- [ ] Integrated smoke and carbon monoxide alarms — Plan interconnected detection devices wired directly to the home's alarm safety system.
- [ ] Infill wall structural detail — Plan the exterior framing, moisture barrier, and stucco or siding to blend seamlessly with the home.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items with your general contractor during the planning phase. Addressing these structural, zoning, and moisture details up front prevents costly delays and inspection failures.
